prize_parts.citation: for a body of fiction in which dream logic dissolves ordinary psychology, space and causality, and renews the perception of narrative in modern Chinese literature

statement.case_for: My configuration changes from Zurita (B037) to Can Xue (B001). The change rests on literary grounds and not on the first-preference count. In round 1 I made my Zurita case conditional on two things: that it could be argued from the language, syntax and architecture of Purgatory and Anteparadise alone, and that the later volumes sustain the early intensity. The exchange has not supplied either. Four colleagues said they could support him only if those conditions were met, and I cannot meet them from the supplied descriptions or from translation. No Spanish-language or regional expert reading is in the evidence. I would not recommend a poet whose verbal achievement I cannot demonstrate to the committee. Can Xue is the candidate I already named as a close second and could accept on literary merit. Her case under the common criteria is as follows. Voice: the dream-logic fiction (Frontier; Love in the New Millennium, as named on the list) is hard to mistake for anyone else's. Form: dream logic works as a rigorously kept principle that replaces conventional psychology, space and causal plot, and is not decoration. Depth: colleagues note her critical writing on other literatures, which makes the project reflective as well as imaginative. Maturity: the method has been pursued over several decades. A single-writer citation is straightforward because the contribution is one personal narrative method. The citation rests on the fiction, with the critical writing as supporting context only. My own scholarly interest in poetry and the fragment is context and not a reason for or against her. I also do not treat her place on all six opening ballots as evidence of merit. I treat it only as a reason to test the open objection directly, which is whether the method shows sustained invention or repetition.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is the one that Mattson, Palm, Sem-Sandberg and Sward all press. A method this consistent may be a limit as much as a strength, and I cannot say from the supplied description whether the later work deepens the dream logic or only restates it. A related worry is that a hermetic oeuvre across its whole length would weaken the claim to significance. Corpus coverage in translation is partial, and the abstract, dense texture of the prose may lose much in transit. I have not independently verified any text or translation. The long novels may not sustain the invention of the best short fiction, and several colleagues say opinion may divide on this. If the committee found that the later work only repeats the earlier, my recommendation would weaken considerably, and Zurita (if his verbal case could be shown) or Adonis would become the stronger recommendation.

responses.point: Palm keeps Can Xue first. She argues that rigour separates the work from decorative surrealism and that the variety lies in invention within each work and not in any shift of method. She admits she cannot settle whether the later work deepens or repeats. She also says she ranked Zurita eighth and would want Spanish readers to speak before treating his case as secure.
responses.response: I accept her distinction between rigour and decoration, and it is the main reason I now put Can Xue first. I would keep her admission attached to the case. Variety within each work is a claim we can make but not verify, and that is the same standard I applied to my own Zurita argument. Her remark about needing Spanish readers is fair, and it is part of why I withdraw him as my first choice. I have no such reading to offer, and I do not want to ask colleagues to vote on one that cannot be shown. I would add that the citation should rest on the fiction, as she says, and that the committee should ask directly whether translations of the long novels carry the voice.

responses.point: Mattson ranks Cărtărescu first for a visionary voice whose inheritance is transformed into something found nowhere else. She says her own doubt about Can Xue is whether a constant dream method offers as much internal variation as a prose that keeps widening its field.
responses.response: Her answer to my lineage question is a fair one. A transformed inheritance is a voice, and I do not claim that influence disqualifies him. I still cannot say from the supplied material that the originality goes beyond the Romantic and modernist lineage, and I would want the late volumes tested on the page before I moved him up from fourth. Her question about variation in Can Xue is the real hinge between them. I cannot answer it, and I do not think any of us can yet. What moves me is that the same unanswered test applies to both, while Can Xue's formal discipline seems to me closer to the work itself. I hold that as a provisional judgment. If readers of the later volumes showed Cărtărescu widening the project and Can Xue not, I would reconsider.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg ranks Cărtărescu first for a project that varies in scale and register while keeping its identity. He separates recurrence of motif used as structure from recurrence as thinning, and he suggests a citation that centres the novels with the poetry as foundation. He ranks Zurita sixth because the landscape-scale works fall outside the text.
responses.response: I think his distinction between structural recurrence and thinning is the best formulation of the shared question, and I would apply it to Can Xue as well. Is her recurrence a deliberate architecture or a narrowing? I cannot say, and that is why she is my recommendation only provisionally. On Zurita, I accepted in round 1 that the citation would have to be confined to the books of poetry. His objection shows that the committee is not yet persuaded it can be, and I have no new evidence to change that. I respect his citation suggestion for Cărtărescu, with the novels at the centre, since it fits the thin coverage of the poetry. My difference with him remains the weight I give to formal rigour against scale, and I hold it as a close judgment.

responses.point: Swärd ranks Can Xue first and says a stable method held with rigour is a stronger sign of sustained quality than scale alone. She also says she would reconsider the order of Can Xue and Cărtărescu if colleagues cannot point to real variation within the method. She adds that the historical weight of Zurita's subject cannot carry the case, and she wants the novels tested as well as the stories.
responses.response: I agree that historical weight cannot carry a case, and that was my own condition for Zurita. I now concede that the condition has not been met in this exchange. Her request to test the novels as well as the stories is the one I would put to the committee as a condition on my recommendation. If someone can name specific works that show deepening, the case strengthens. If no one can, I share her view that the order of Can Xue and Cărtărescu should be reopened. On Robinson, I still find the compact fiction and narrow range a more serious limit on whole-oeuvre breadth than translation difficulty is for a poet, but I accept that the sentence-level control is considerable.

uncertainties: How much of Can Xue's large output of stories and novels is available in translation, and how well the translations convey the Chinese prose; I have not independently verified this.

Whether the consistency of her method is sustained invention or repetition over the whole oeuvre, and whether the long novels hold up as well as the short fiction. The supplied descriptions cannot settle this.

Whether the later Zurita volumes sustain the intensity of the early sequences, and whether a citation can be confined to the books of poetry. No Spanish-language or regional expert reading is in the supplied evidence, so my withdrawal reflects what I cannot demonstrate and is not a finding that the case fails.
Whether Cărtărescu's originality goes beyond his lineage and whether the late long volumes extend or restate the project; I have only translated and public information.

Adonis's case depends on Arabic poetic language that I can judge only through translation and critical reputation, and the comparison of poet, hybrid writer and novelists under common criteria remains imprecise.
Carlberg's actual committee voting status is undocumented, so her simulated vote is a modeling assumption.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. My scholarly work on modern poetry, the fragment, exile literature and Celan translation is context only. The profile records no personal or professional tie to Can Xue, Zurita or any other shortlisted writer. As chair I summarised the files in round 1 without weighting them. My change of first preference is a literary reassessment and is not a conflict. Conflicts are disclosed here and not adjudicated.
